title: Borobudur
summary: Borobudur, in the Kedu Valley of Central Java, is a Buddhist stupa built in the 8th and 9th centuries CE under the Syailendra dynasty. Five square terraces and three circular platforms rise around a hill to a central stupa, 72 smaller openwork stupas each hold a Buddha, and carved reliefs cover the walls. It was restored with UNESCO's help in the 1970s.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO says Borobudur was built in the 8th and 9th centuries AD during the Syailendra Dynasty and gives no more exact years; the start year 701 is the first year of the 8th century, so the true start is later within that span. End is the present.

phases.description: Built in the 8th and 9th centuries AD during the Syailendra Dynasty (UNESCO); no finer dates are given in the sources opened.

The ruins were found by the British lieutenant-governor Raffles in 1814 (UNESCO, Japanese-language description). When and why the monument fell out of use is not given in the sources opened; this phase starts where recorded construction ends.
Restored with UNESCO's help in the 1970s and inscribed as a World Heritage property.

reviewer_note: Shape stupa: UNESCO calls the main temple 'a stupa built in three tiers', so stupa fits better than stepped_pyramid. Least sure of the dates (UNESCO gives only 'the 8th and 9th centuries'; 701 and 900 are the span, not claims) and of the 900-1970 'ruined' phase, whose start is unsourced; it is bridged only because the 1814 discovery of ruins shows it stood. Base 120 m a side is JAXA's; an e-museum copy of a UNESCO publication gives 113 m (123 m overall with projections) and 'nearly 35 m' high, which agrees on height. The 1814 reference appears only in the Japanese text of UNESCO's page.
